findings.detail: `retiredModels` is a module-level Set and `retireModel()` strikes an id off for the whole session across every tier and every key. The PR's own reasoning in `verifyGeminiKey` (services/geminiService.ts:128-131) states the opposite premise for that function — "model availability is per key and per project" — and deliberately refuses to record there for exactly this reason. The real call paths do record. The app explicitly supports multiple keys (`rotateKey()` reorders them, `getStoredApiKey()` returns `geminiKeys[0]`, and TranslateTab's own partial message tells users to "add more API keys (one per line)"), and Gemini returns a NOT_FOUND/404 for a model the *project behind that key* cannot use — which `isModelUnavailable()` cannot distinguish from a genuine retirement. Concrete failure: a user has two keys, key B's project lacks `gemini-3.1-pro`. A 429 on key A rotates to key B, key B's next call 404s on `gemini-3.1-pro`, and the id is struck off for the rest of the session — so every later Translate/OCR/Compare/Web-Scraper call runs on a weaker model even after rotation puts key A back in front. It self-corrects on reload and the fallback still produces output, which is why this is medium rather than high; it would be high if the retirement were persisted (it deliberately is not, per the comment at services/geminiService.ts:53-60).
findings.summary: Session-global model retirement is keyed on the model only, not the key that failed

findings.detail: The workbook banner twelve lines above (components/TranslateTab.tsx:534-539) branches on `mode === 'separate'` precisely so a separate-mode user is not sent hunting for text that was never written — the comment at :529-533 says so explicitly. The in-app log message added in the same block does not branch: it states unconditionally "untranslated rows keep their original text". In `separate` mode without `mergeSource`, an untranslated row's target column is written as `tText` = `""` (components/TranslateTab.tsx:446), so the log contradicts both the workbook and the code. The log is the message the user actually reads first, in the session where they can still act on it.
findings.summary: Partial-run log claims original text is kept, which is false in `separate` mode

findings.detail: The comment that used to sit above `const model = GEMINI_PRO;` survived the deletion of that line and now makes two claims the code no longer supports. It opens "Pro, by request" while `model` is `resolveModel('quality')`, which can legitimately be a Flash id once a Pro id is struck off — the degradation this PR exists to enable. It closes with "roughly three minutes before TranslateTab logs the error and stops", but TranslateTab no longer stops: it `break`s, exports a PARTIAL_-prefixed workbook, and sets ERROR (components/TranslateTab.tsx:352-371, 550). This codebase leans on comments as its primary documentation — every other comment in this diff was updated with care — so a stale one here is the kind that gets trusted and mis-plans the next change.
findings.summary: translateBatch's comment block now describes behaviour the PR changed

findings.detail: The model registry got 26 tests; the guard that this PR describes as preventing "silent corruption: plausible translations attached to the wrong products, invisible in the output" got none. It is the highest-consequence branch added here (a short array from the model would otherwise mis-file every result after the gap) and it is the one whose regression is invisible — reverting `translations.length !== currentBatchItems.length` to a bare `forEach` leaves every existing test green and produces output that looks correct. The same applies to the empty-result filter at :325-331 and the `processedUniqueCount` / `isPartial` derivation at :493-494, which the PR's own comments flag as previously miscounting.
findings.summary: The batch length-mismatch guard — the silent-corruption fix — has no test
